objective: Test whether one multiscale graph-smoothness statistic can combine fine-scale best-candidate sensitivity with stable full-panel ordering across linear, quadratic, local, and periodic continuous targets.

ancestry.outcome_use: The prior artifact motivated the fixed formulation only. All ranking outcomes use new panel seeds and are recomputed from frozen generators and heads.

reference_heads.envelope: Maximum held-out R2 across the four frozen nested-tuned head families.

shared_execution.folds: One four-fold shuffled KFold partition per panel, shared across every candidate and geometry; random_state equals panel seed.
shared_execution.target_scaling: Training-fold target scaler fitted by ContinuousOverlapIndex; held-out targets transformed without refit.

graph.distance: Squared Euclidean distance in the fitted held-out geometry.
graph.neighbor_ties: Stable row-index order resolves exact distance ties.
graph.self_tuning_weight: exp(-squared_distance_ij / (sigma_i * sigma_j)), where sigma_i is Euclidean distance to row i's 15th neighbor and a deterministic positive floor handles duplicates.

score.scale_actual_loss: Weighted mean absolute scaled-target difference over the directed k-neighbor edges.
score.scale_null: Mean loss from 32 global permutations of held-out scaled targets on the identical edges and weights.
score.integrated_score: Fixed weighted arithmetic mean of the three bounded scale scores.

decision_rule.undefined_spearman: Any constant selector or undefined panel correlation fails completeness; undefined values are retained as null and never omitted from eligibility.
decision_rule.interpretation: A candidate must satisfy every absolute, matched-current-OI, linear-probe-regret, periodic-gain, family-preservation, and completeness condition.

selection_tie_rule: Average reference performance across candidates tied for maximum selector value at absolute tolerance 1e-12.
scope: Exploratory new-seed synthetic test. A pass permits a separately frozen broader validation only; it does not authorize public integration or a generalization claim.
